Q251.summary: Essentially the same change as Q136: moves the generated-ref exemption before the relpath rule and resolves exhaustion override refs in the loop executor from 2.29.

why.cause: control_loops.py::_exhausted_inactive_placeholder_values no longer emits the redundant, validator-forbidden relpath placeholder, which fixes the compile error at its source. why.fit: The compiler is the right layer for what gets emitted, but the patch flips a deliberate target gate instead of reusing a runtime resolution mechanism.

Q331.summary: Stops emitting exhaustion placeholders for relpath fields and makes union loop results read on-exhausted state fields directly at every target.

why.cause: validation.py::_validate_repeat_until_on_exhausted admits generated relpath refs, and loops.py::repeat_until_exhaustion_artifacts resolves the override refs where the frame is built.
why.contracts: Resolution is not version-gated, so persisted exhausted frames also change at 2.28 and earlier. A resolution error returns None, which silently turns into an ordinary repeat_until_iterations_exhausted failure. It also adds projection metadata to every 2.29+ union match case in control_loops.py.
why.generality: Own-frame refs are resolved through build_loop_scope, whose root_steps point at the persisted running frame rather than the exhaustion snapshot from _exhaustion_frame_artifacts. For loops with max 2 or more, state-projected fields such as rounds can therefore differ from what 2.28 returns.
why.fit: Two parallel mechanisms (runtime resolution plus skipping inactive case outputs in lowering) address one problem, and the scope used does not match the frame being finalized.

why.cause: The frame still stores raw {ref} dicts. executor.py::_resolve_structured_output_artifacts only chases them when the source is a LoopOutputAddress, which treats the symptom at one consumer.

why.fit: It puts legacy ref-chain following into the typed bound-address path, which _resolve_runtime_value deliberately refuses ("Typed runtime does not accept legacy ref payloads"), instead of resolving at the producer in loops.py.
